title: T196 PNC - Do Not Make Your Prayer Fixed — Pray with Mercy and Supplication
hebrewTitle: אל תעש תפילתך קבע אלא רחמים ותחנונים
author: Petten Nanach

beginner.en: "Do not make your prayer fixed, but mercy and supplications" (Avot 2:13). It is forbidden to demand from Hashem — to insist that He must grant what you want. Prayer must be approached as a beggar approaches a king: with complete vulnerability, with mercy-seeking, not with demands. The moment prayer becomes a fixed formula or a contract with expectations, it loses its essential quality. True prayer is always fresh, always from a place of genuine need and trust, never from entitlement. You ask, but the King decides — and that relationship is itself the prayer.

intermediate.en: T196: "Al taaseh tefillatecha keva" (Avot 2:13) — prayer must not be demand-based (kivyachol obligating Hashem) but merciful supplication (rachamim v'tachanunin). The petitioner is a pauper before the King; demanding is a categorical error. LM 196.
intermediate.he: אסור לאדם לתבוע מה׳ בתפילה. תפילה צריכה להיות כעני המבקש רחמים, לא כמי שדורש חוב. "אל תעש תפילתך קבע" (אבות ב:יג).

scholarly.he: LM א׳ קצ״ו — אבות ב:יג "אל תעש תפילתך קבע אלא רחמים ותחנונים"; אסור לדרוש מה׳ בתפילה.
